scope: Theorem 4.5 (Domain-independent decaying trajectory) of the manuscript “SLE3 universality for weak finite-range Ising interactions” (preprints/SLE3-universality-for-weak-finite-range-Ising-interactions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 44a7837e35328259), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 37-38. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every J > 0 and finite-range real potential U satisfying the symmetries of Theorem 1.1, the preceding scale parameters can be fixed 37 independently of all domains and boundary data. The initial scale s0 may be enlarged by any prescribed finite amount before the following construction. For each sufficiently small ϵ > 0 there is λ∗ > 0 and a real analytic function βc : (−λ∗, λ∗) → (0, ∞), with βc(0) = β0, for which the initial potential (4.23) has a trajectory Vk+1 = Φsk (Vk) satisfying ∥Vk∥sk,d ≤ ϵ2−k , k ≥ 0. (4.24) Its intermediate one-step trajectories obey sup 0≤t≤1 ∑ ℓ |ℓ|e(d/2)(|ℓ|−1) ∥vk,ℓ(t)∥∞ ≤ Cϵ2−k . (4.25) The same construction applies to both signs of λ.
